editorial.summary: Chapter 25 is both a three-hour relationship autopsy and the clearest internal product critique so far. Asa says a useful podcast needs accurate descriptive titles, 25–45 minute topical paths, a short opening, two or three intelligible speakers, excellent audio and something informative; DVDASA instead sounds like an overheard party in a blank, echoing room. The archive should preserve that long-form social texture while adding the access layer the cast wanted: complete audio, speaker-focused views, reliable chapters, searchable topics, corrections and an optional short path. The episode then announces a family of satellite formats—Billy Bob Crit, Stevie, a proposed Choe/Chang show, a solo Choe Show and an Asa show—rather than an actual breakup. The central account begins around October 25 and November 2, 2014. David Choe and Nikki Skyler directly describe an ambiguous open relationship, a stated no-friends boundary, his expiration date and partner-count disclosures, his neglect and public disavowal during the November 2 event, her sex with an unnamed artist she says she did not know was his friend, his anger and retaliatory behavior, a threesome framed as restitution, her no-contact boundary with the third participant, his later violation of it, mutual social-media retaliation, renewed sex and a proposal to abolish rules that is ultimately rejected. The record does not decide who is morally right, identify the artist or third participant, reproduce private texts, or convert fantasy language into standing consent. It preserves direct disagreement: witnesses saw conversation but not the claimed information exchange; the host asserts sexual details and then admits some are unknown; both people acknowledge harmful behavior and different understandings of their status. Choking, slapping, threats, coercive framing, blood/semen eye exposure, unsafe anal-sex pseudo-instruction and stigmatizing STI claims receive separate safety context without censoring the speech. Source leads include the November 2 AMA/live event, Billy Bob Crit, Momofuku Ko art, Andy Milonakis, Joe Rogan, Mangchi's second album, proposed satellite shows, Blind Date with Salie and the Mangchi outro. The final music contains decoder repetition and uncertain lyrics; no words are invented. Line-level speaker names remain withheld until held-out acoustic validation passes.
